outcome: Four named native documentation procedures use a separate DocsRpcGroup and DocsRpcClient with revision 1. The combined server supplies thirteen procedures; the nine calculator contracts and their revision 4 are preserved.

The content owner supplies a bounded canonical public-page address and fixed public missing-page/search errors to both HTTP and RPC. Existing HTTP error exports, status/media behaviour and messages remain; generated OpenAPI records the same canonical page-path bound on replies.

Each native documentation operation owns its receive-loop scope, a ten-second headers-and-body deadline and the existing two-MiB reply-byte limit. Credentials are omitted, redirects rejected, RPC and HTTP tracing disabled.

Only native reply-decoding defects become DocsRpcInvalidResponse. An independent HTTP-adapter SchemaError retains exact defect identity. Expected source errors become fixed public errors without source diagnostics.

The installed native RPC global fatal path retains the existing safe literal Calculation service failed. Procedure Exit defect encoding uses Documentation service failed. Both remain defects; mixed interruption/defect Causes retain no raw diagnostic on the wire.

The ordinary compiled Node reader and actual built local native API compare owning navigation, all 61 page values and byte-equal processed Markdown. The retained website native-pair corpus remains eleven cases; this slice does not connect production Website documentation routes.

priorFailureAndRecovery: Old calculator server fixtures initially lacked the ContentService now required by the combined server; they supply the owning checked controlled catalogue. Actual package output needed rebuilding after shared error ownership changed.

Native protocol fixtures initially used the wrong URL prefix and tracing context; they now use the installed native protocol contract and explicit tracing-disabled service. A tap callback now returns an Effect.

Focused lint rejected unsorted keys, direct collection indexing, wire-fixture encoding and tagged-error factory syntax outside the admitted paths. Narrow exact-file decoder/contract/egress/factory permissions now mirror the actual operations; neighbouring paths and Effect runners remain rejected.

An automatic lint correction incorrectly changed new tagged-error class definitions. The source was corrected and exact factory exemptions added; type/lint and the actual CLI fixture corpus then pass.

An initial fatal-reply test incorrectly expected DocsRpcInvalidResponse. Inspection of the installed native client/server showed that fatal defects retain Cause semantics. Controlled native fatal and mixed procedure Exit wire cases now prove fixed safe literals without converting defects into expected errors.
The first lint-fixture insertion was placed in a string-only file loop. It was moved to the exact native RPC fixture table; tools types and all 572 actual CLI fixtures pass.

Knip rejected a duplicate public reply-limit alias. The alias was removed and the existing CalculatorRpcResponseLimit remains the sole constant. Production Knip initially saw the stale compiled alias; rebuilding the actual graph removes it and production Knip passes.
